issue.title: test_capacity_gate_to_admission: land directive queue_weight is None where 2.0 is expected (2 tests)
issue.description:
# CI failure: test_capacity_gate_to_admission - land directive queue_weight is None

## CI failure

- **Node:** `tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission`
- **Node:** `tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py::test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget`

Both fail deterministically with `assert None == 2.0` on `land.queue_weight` (the land segment of a
rendered epic plan has `PromptDirectives.queue_weight` of `None` where the test expects `2.0`;
`weight_explicit=False`). Reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_32 at master `244442ee8` in the
full lane, in isolation, and again with the working tree's `src/` changes reverted to `HEAD`.

Root cause NOT established. Candidates: `89d51301f` (`feat: adopt queue capacity budget adapters`,
touched the directive expansion; the tests were last touched by `14ddd4d82`), or a sase-core
mismatch: this workspace's `_setup` rebuilt `sase_core_rs` 0.34.63 -> 0.34.66 from the linked
sase-core checkout, and the weight default may live on the Rust side. Check which side computes
the land weight before fixing.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: same 'assert None == 2.0' in the full lane, in isolation, and with the working tree's src reverted to HEAD; both tests in the file fail the same way.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced by the sase-zr.7 land agent on 2026-09-20 at master 6087c0a8e in the full just test-scoped lane (43678 passed, 4 failed): both test_capacity_gate_to_admission nodes are among the four. Phase sase-zr.7.3 had already recorded them as failing on its baseline, so this predates and is independent of that phase's diff. Note sase-13q is a same-day duplicate report of this bead.

payload.entry:
DUPLICATE MERGED IN: sase-13q (filed 4m51s later, athena workspace sase_31) is closed as superseded by this bead. Carrying forward the unique evidence it held, which this bead lacked:

1. Commit attribution by replay: run per commit in a detached worktree with PYTHONPATH pointed at it, both nodes fail at 244442ee8, 9cfb06a54, 9231c9352, 65c8169f9 and e65cc22ee, so the failure predates all five most recent commits at the time. It also carried 8 corroborating reports from independent agents (sase-iu, 0ny--code, 0nv.f0--code and others), all with the same assert None == 2.0 on land.queue_weight.
2. Pointer: the %queue directive wiring landed in 0770357cd, and the test file was last touched by 89d51301f 'feat: adopt queue capacity budget adapters'.
3. Its open questions -- whether installed plugins or user xprompt config change how bd/land_epic expands, and whether sase-core skew matters -- are answered by the root cause recorded in the next note.

Still failing at master ec7dbbfdf (2 failed, verified 2026-09-20 in athena workspace sase_34), so this bead stays open.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-09-20 triage, athena workspace sase_34, master ec7dbbfdf). Neither candidate the bead named is responsible: it is not sase-core skew, not the installed plugin set, and not user xprompt config.

The land segment never receives a queue weight because render_multi_prompt never asks for one. src/sase/bead/work.py builds the land segment (around line 480) and calls _queue_capacity_lines(...), which calls format_queue_directive(capacity=capacity) and passes no weight -- see src/sase/bead/work.py:507-515. src/sase/xprompt/queue_directive.py:104 accepts weight= and would render it, so the field exists and is simply never populated. With capacity=3 the land segment therefore emits %q:3 and expands to PromptDirectives(queue_weight=None, queue_weight_explicit=False), exactly the observed failure. When capacity is omitted, _queue_capacity_lines returns [] and no %queue line is emitted at all, which is why the second node, test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget, fails the same way: its name says the land weight must survive an omitted capacity, so the expected weight cannot be derived from capacity.

Ruled out by direct check: the xprompt body cannot supply it either. bd/land_epic is a built-in xprompt from src/sase/default_config.yml, and expanding '#bd/land_epic:sase-zp' in-process yields queue_weight=None with no %queue directive in the body -- correctly so, since tests/test_bead_xprompt_tags.py::test_bead_worker_builtin_xprompts_do_not_author_wait_directives forbids built-in bead-worker xprompts from authoring wait/queue directives. So the weight must come from the renderer, not the prompt text.

Open decision for the worker (do not just loosen the assertion): whether a land agent is contractually supposed to claim weight 2.0 against the weighted-load budget. tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py:152-154 asserts land.queue_weight == 2.0 with land.queue_weight_explicit True while phase.queue_weight_explicit is False, and those assertions came in with 14ddd4d82 'docs(queue): document weighted capacity and verify gate-to-admission path' (sase-zp.4), whose docs/xprompt.md changes describe the weighted-load model. Either (a) the contract is real and _queue_capacity_lines must emit the land weight unconditionally of capacity, or (b) 14ddd4d82 documented an intent that was never implemented and the test is wrong. Settle it from the docs that commit wrote and from docs/xprompt.md's current weighted-capacity section, then fix one side with a justification.
